title: SRE on-call scratchpad - DB failover follow-ups
content:
Context:
- Night shift paging event at 01:13 UTC: primary write DB (postgres-cluster-prod) degraded and failed leader election during heavy KV cache warm-up.
- Pager: high error rate (502/504) on hosted API route /v1/generate for ~7 minutes. External alerts: SLO-error-rate > 5% (5min). Internal alert: PG replica lag > 30s.
- Incident ID: INC-2026-142, on-call triage at 01:15 UTC (me + noah), handover to db-eng at 01:22 UTC.

Timeline (quick):
- 01:13 UTC: Pager fires (error spikes).
- 01:15 UTC: I start triage - connect to primary, see postgres stuck in promotion loop (repeated timeline: StartPromote -> fail -> retry).
- 01:18 UTC: Confirmed I/O errors on disk /dev/nvme1n1 on primary host (short spikes).
- 01:22 UTC: Escalated to db-eng (Lena) and opened INC-2026-142. Began redirecting read traffic to replicas and enabling fallback model-route.
- 01:27 UTC: Manual failover initiated by db-eng to replica-2; promotion completed at 01:34 UTC.
- 01:36 UTC: Traffic shifted back; error rate trended down to baseline by 01:40 UTC.
- 02:05 UTC: Post-incident checks: replication healthy, KV cache warmed but still < ideal for some hosts -> transient latencies.

What I did (actions):
- Confirmed alert and collected initial logs (pg logs, kernel dmesg, iostat) from primary. Saved to /inc/INC-2026-142/artifacts/ (sftp link in ticket).
- Added temporary route rule in edge (route: hosted-api -> model-variant fallback) to reduce tail errors while DB was promoted.
- Notified customers on status page (short note) and Slack #prod-alerts.
- Coordinated manual failover and validated read/write resiliency post-promotion.

Immediate follow-ups / TODOs (owner, ETA):
- [ ] (db-eng) Investigate root cause of NVMe I/O spikes (Lena) - ETA 2026-03-24 - linked to INC-2026-142.
- [ ] (infra) Add SMART + NVMe metrics to host monitoring and set threshold alert for >10% I/O latency spikes (Noah) - ETA 2026-03-27.
- [ ] (me) Update runbook: clarify manual failover steps and include exact commands we ran; add checklist for route fallbacks and customer comms - ETA 2026-03-22.
- [ ] (sre) Create replay job to re-run cache warm-up against promoted host to validate KV warm-up sequence - ETA 2026-03-25.
- [ ] (ops) Validate backups and PITR window for the affected DB (owner: backup-eng) - ETA 2026-03-23.

Runbook gaps found (notes to update):
- Failover section vague on when to shift edge routing to fallback model (add thresholds: >3% 5m error rate OR DB replication lag >20s).
- Lacks explicit check commands for NVMe health; add iostat, nvme-cli examples and where to store outputs.
- No dedicated step for communicating with CS/customer-success (add template for status page + Slack + email).

Artifacts to attach to postmortem:
- pg logs (primary) 01:00-02:00 UTC (inc/artifacts/pg-primary-2026-03-20.log)
- dmesg + kernel messages showing I/O errors (inc/artifacts/dmesg-2026-03-20.log)
- iostat and sar for primary host (inc/artifacts/iostat-sar-2026-03-20.tar)
- edge route change diff + timestamps (git commit / PR link in ticket)
- Metrics graphs: error rate, p99 latency, replica lag (Grafana links in ticket)

Immediate manual checks I want to run next run (short list):
- Re-run nvme smart health on primary host and the rest of the cluster.
- Verify cold-start behavior for KV cache: simulate restart on a canary host and measure p50/p95 token latencies during warm-up.
- Ensure autoscaling for dedicated pools didn't throttle during promotion window.

Handoff notes for next on-call (morning):
- Incident INC-2026-142 resolved; postmortem in progress.
- Primary cause likely NVMe I/O spikes causing promotion loop -> manual failover. db-eng investigating.
- Runbook updates queued (see TODOs) - priority: runbook update + monitoring threshold for NVMe.
- Customer comms: initial status page posted; will update postmortem summary once ready.

Misc scratch TODOs (personal quick list):
- [ ] Draft short postmortem summary for Slack #sre-ops (aim for 2 paragraphs).
- [ ] Add runbook code snippets and verify in staging.
- [ ] Follow up with Lena on RCA findings next Wed standup.
- [ ] File infra ticket for SMART alerting (link to create).

Notes / observations:
- Spike happened during high traffic warm-up window (01:10-01:20 UTC) - consider staggering cache re-warm for large capacity changes.
- Edge fallback helped reduce customer impact quickly; make fallback route more discoverable in the runbook.

End of notes.
